current.text: Curry has said publicly that his knee issue is a new normal.
Several experts are worried about the health of his knee, and it is the main reason he is ranked below his per-game level.
He projects as a top 12 to 13 player per game in categories this season.
His fair draft range in category leagues is picks 20 to 30. Taking him around pick 23 is fine.
In an auction, Josh values him at about 40 USD per game but would not pay more than 25 USD because of the knee, other injuries and the weak Warriors roster. He went for 26 USD in that mock.
He is still one of the best players in the league at age 38.
Golden State has no shot creator besides Curry, so he is expected to carry a huge offensive load.
The Warriors are reportedly treating this season as a gap year and may rest veterans to protect their lottery odds.
The team may be bad enough to cut his minutes, and Warriors players are expected to fade as the season goes on.
Golden State has 15 back-to-backs this season, tied for second most.
The Warriors schedule is good for fantasy playoffs that end March 28.
Golden State has very poor depth and struggles to field a 10-man rotation.

durable.text: He is an elite three-point shooter with steady volume. He made 4.4 threes per game in each of the last two seasons.
He is a high-volume, consistent free throw shooter at about 92 to 93 percent, which lifts a team's FT%.
Points, threes and FT% are his strong categories. His assists and steals do not stand out.
His turnovers are high for a guard.
He is worth much more in category leagues than in points leagues.
He missed games late last season with runner's knee, a wear-and-tear issue.
Injury is the main fantasy risk with Curry. Expect maintenance rest days.

note: Per game, Curry is still a top 12 to 13 category player. He brings elite threes, points and FT%, and his turnovers are high, so he fits punt TO builds. The price question is games played: the knee, his age, 15 back-to-backs and a Warriors team that may rest veterans. Yahoo values him at 31 USD and ESPN at 22 USD. He cost 42 USD in our league last season, and Josh caps him at 25 USD, so aim for about 25 to 30 USD and let others pay last year's price. Early in the season, watch how often he rests on back-to-backs and whether Golden State starts badly enough to lean into the gap year.
